title: No dashes as connectors
instruction: Do not use em dashes or spaced dashes to join clauses or insert asides. State the relation with a comma, colon, parentheses or a new sentence.
context: Editable prose, captions and figure labels. Ranges keep en dashes; compounds keep hyphens; minus signs stay.
rationale: A dash used as the default connector leaves the relation between the parts unstated.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP1 (rules.md, formulaic prose patterns); opt-in.

examples.original: The fit improves — the error falls by a third.
examples.preferred: The fit improves: the error falls by a third.

title: No contrastive framing
instruction: Do not use 'rather than', 'not X but Y' or 'X and not Y'. State the positive claim; when two alternatives are compared, name both and the comparison.
context: Editable prose. Preserve negation, comparison direction and scope when recasting.
rationale: The frame sets a claim against an alternative the text never proposed and adds no information.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP2; opt-in.

examples.original: We fit one constant per mode rather than per city.
examples.preferred: We fit one constant per mode, shared by all cities.

title: No clefts
instruction: Do not use 'It is X that ...' or 'What ... is ...' sentences. Use subject-verb order.
context: Editable prose. Keep conditional force and do not add exclusivity when recasting.
rationale: A cleft delays the claim and adds emphasis the evidence may not support.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP3; opt-in.

examples.original: It is the network, not the waits, that explains most of the gap.
examples.preferred: The network explains most of the gap; the waits explain little of it.

title: At most one colon per sentence
instruction: Use no more than one colon in a prose sentence. Split the sentence or let the verb carry the relation.
context: Prose sentences. Ratios, times, labels, URLs and mathematical notation do not count.
rationale: Chained colons stack announcements and hide the structure of the claim.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP4; opt-in.

examples.original: Two results stand out: first, coverage is low: a third of the stops are missing.
examples.preferred: Two results stand out. First, coverage is low: a third of the stops are missing.

title: No filler or intensifiers
instruction: Remove 'Importantly', 'Notably', 'It is worth noting that', 'plays a crucial role' and emphatic 'essential' or 'key'. State the specific relation or quantity instead.
context: Editable prose. Keep 'key' as a technical term and 'essential' with a stated criterion.
rationale: Emphasis words add length without content and make every sentence equally loud.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP5; opt-in.

examples.original: Importantly, waiting time plays a crucial role in accessibility.
examples.preferred: Waiting time changes accessibility by up to a tenth.

title: No closing restatement
instruction: Delete a final sentence that only repeats the paragraph ('Overall, ...', 'This highlights ...', 'Taken together, ...'). Keep it only when it states a new, supported inference.
rationale: A restatement repeats what the reader has just read.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP6; opt-in.

examples.original: Coverage is lowest in small towns. Overall, this highlights the importance of coverage.
examples.preferred: Coverage is lowest in small towns.

title: No one-sentence paragraphs
instruction: Merge a single-sentence paragraph with the paragraph it serves or develop it into a full paragraph.
context: Body text. Headings, list items and displayed equations are not paragraphs.
rationale: An isolated sentence used for emphasis or transition breaks the argument into fragments.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP7; opt-in.

examples.preferred: Move the sentence into the paragraph that discusses the distribution.

title: No figurative verbs for data and methods
instruction: Do not give data, methods, figures or values human or physical actions ('say', 'answer', 'rest on', 'walk', 'emerge', 'arrive'). Name the operation.
context: Editable prose and captions. Conventional technical subjects such as 'The model predicts' and 'Table 2 lists' stay.
rationale: A figurative verb makes the reader translate it back into the operation that was performed.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP8; opt-in.

examples.original: The ferry estimate rests on four sites.
examples.preferred: The ferry estimate is based on four sites.

title: No placeholder nouns
instruction: Replace 'things', 'aspects', 'issues' and bare numerals used as nouns with the noun they stand for.
context: Editable prose, especially sentences that open a list or refer back to groups.
rationale: A placeholder makes the reader recover a noun the writer already knows.

source.reference: Strict project variant of IDUs FP9; opt-in.

examples.original: Two things follow for anyone using the data.
examples.preferred: Two consequences follow for anyone using the data.
